Package neqsim.process.equipment.network

Class TwoFluidPipeNetwork

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.network.TwoFluidPipeNetwork
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class TwoFluidPipeNetwork extends Object implements Serializable
Phase-conservative transient hydraulic network of TwoFluidPipe branches.

Every branch is advanced from the pressures at the beginning of the network step. Gas, oil, and water boundary transfers are then accumulated at each compressible node, and all node pressures are advanced simultaneously. Fixed-pressure nodes represent external reservoirs or sinks. This explicit storage-node coupling supports splits, merges, manifolds, and injection branches without making branch execution order part of the pressure solution.

This first network layer is intentionally storage based. Algebraic zero-volume junctions, global Newton pressure-flow iteration, and branch subcycling are outside its current scope. Component and total-energy mixing are available as an explicit opt-in on compressible nodes. Signed outlet fallback is supported only when the downstream node or pipe owns an explicit thermodynamic donor.

    • addCompressibleNode

    • addConservativeCompressibleNode

      public void addConservativeCompressibleNode(String nodeName, UpstreamCompressibleVolume volume, SystemInterface initialFluid)
      Add a storage node with conservative named-component and total-energy inventory.

      The existing UpstreamCompressibleVolume remains the hydraulic pressure and phase-mass owner. The supplied fluid defines the component slate, composition and caloric state of the same total node mass. During a network step, every outgoing branch sees one frozen start-of-step node state; all accepted branch transfers are then applied simultaneously. This makes merge and split routing independent of branch insertion order.

      Parameters:
      nodeName - unique node name
      volume - existing hydraulic storage model
      initialFluid - initial node composition and caloric state

    • setConservativeNodeSourceThermodynamics

      public void setConservativeNodeSourceThermodynamics(String nodeName, SystemInterface sourceFluid, double specificEnthalpyJPerKg)
      Define the thermodynamic state of mass entering a conservative storage node through its hydraulic source terms.

      The phase-resolved source rates remain owned by UpstreamCompressibleVolume. This contract supplies the named-component composition and open-system specific enthalpy required to apply the same accepted source mass to the node's component and total-energy inventories. The fluid is defensively copied and later mutations do not change the source definition.

      Parameters:
      nodeName - existing conservative compressible node
      sourceFluid - source composition; its flow rate is ignored
      specificEnthalpyJPerKg - source specific enthalpy in J/kg

    • addFixedPressureNode

      public void addFixedPressureNode(String nodeName, double pressurePa, SystemInterface boundaryFluid)
      Add an external fixed-pressure node with an explicit thermodynamic boundary state.

      The fluid is defensively copied and supplies composition, density and enthalpy only when a connected pipe accepts signed outlet fallback from this node. Pressure remains owned by pressurePa. Forward pipe outflow is unaffected. Use setBranchOutletPhaseBackflowAllowed(String, boolean) to opt a branch into signed fallback.

      Parameters:
      nodeName - unique node name
      pressurePa - fixed mechanical pressure in Pa
      boundaryFluid - thermodynamic state of material entering the network from this node

    • setBranchOutletPhaseBackflowAllowed

      public void setBranchOutletPhaseBackflowAllowed(String branchName, boolean allow)
      Enable or disable signed outlet fallback on one branch using its downstream node as thermodynamic owner.

      A conservative storage node publishes its frozen start-of-step inventory. A fixed-pressure node must have been created with an explicit boundary fluid. The donor is installed before the pipe option is enabled, preserving the pipe's fail-closed configuration contract.

      Parameters:
      branchName - existing branch name
      allow - true to permit signed outlet fallback
